prompt:
Pixel art emblem of the zodiac sign LEO: a lion's head seen from the front, the mane a full circle of broad pointed locks like the rays of the sun, the face a simple shield shape with a long straight nose; a small plain crown of three points rests on the brow.

Layout, the same as the other emblems in this set: a thin-lined regular hexagon frame (all six sides equal, point at the top), large, almost touching the edges of the square image. The emblem sits in the middle and fills most of the hexagon, overlapping its outline slightly. Behind the hexagon, straight golden sun rays, long and short in turn, spread outward past the frame on all sides, like the sunburst behind a sun emblem.

This is a SYMBOL, not a character: a timeless emblem like a heraldic crest, a carved totem or a stained-glass roundel. Front-facing, perfectly symmetrical left to right, still and dignified, so that anyone born under the sign can see themselves in it. No cartoon expression, no mascot, no cuteness, no story. Never fierce or scary. The face is calm and neutral with a steady level gaze: no roar, no open mouth, no fangs, no snarl, no frown. The sign's nature shows only through form: a full round radiating mane, a high broad brow, an upright bearing: warmth, generosity, pride, a heart like the sun.

Style: bold simplified geometric shapes with thick dark outlines between them, 16-bit console pixel art, hard square pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering. Drawn on a 96 x 96 pixel grid, shown enlarged so each pixel is a clear square. The whole image has a flat solid BLACK background, edge to edge.

Palette: exactly four flat colours plus black: cream, golden yellow, burnt orange, royal purple. At most two flat shades of each, nothing else.

Square image, no text, no letters, no watermark, no signature.
